# Grade 7 Life Science Unit Plan: Cellular Respiration & Photosynthesis
Instructor: Marcus Vance | Room 204 | Quarter 3, Week 5 (02/09/2026 - 02/13/2026)

## Target Standards and Alignment
| Standard Code | Focus Description | Mastery Metric |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MS-LS1-6 | Photosynthesis matter cycling and energy flow | 80% on lab analysis rubrics |
| MS-LS1-7 | Chemical reaction of cellular respiration in cells | Proficient on end-of-unit CER |

## Weekly Objectives and Student-Facing Targets
- Monday: Introduce photosynthesis equation. SWBAT write the chemical equation for photosynthesis showing light energy converting into stored chemical energy.
- Student-facing board prompt: I can define the products of photosynthesis and explain how plants destroy energy during glucose formation.
- Tuesday: Photosynthesis elodea bubble investigation. SWBAT collect quantitative rate data by measuring oxygen production at variable light distances.
- Wednesday: Cellular respiration overview. SWBAT compare reactants and products of aerobic respiration across animal and plant cells.
- Student-facing board prompt: I can trace how oxygen and glucose produce carbon dioxide, water, and ATP.
- Thursday: Formative check. SWBAT demonstrate mastery by scoring at least on the 10-question midpoint check.
- Friday: Energy pyramid and nutrient transfer synthesis. SWBAT model how cellular respiration transfers thermal and chemical energy through trophic tiers.

## Student Communication & Tracking
- Post daily learning targets in student-friendly "I can" phrasing on the west whiteboard prior to 07:45 AM daily.
- Require students to record the target in their science notebooks during the initial 5-minute bell-ringer window.
- Administer the MS-LS1-2 summative assessment on Friday afternoon to measure cellular respiration mastery.

errors.explanation: This violates the foundational law of conservation of energy taught in MS-LS1-6, which states energy cannot be created or destroyed, contradicting the standard's focus on energy flow and conversion.
errors.fix: explain how plants convert light energy into chemical energy during glucose formation
